reason: Conversation 2 stays concise, asks one thing at a time, keeps safety in view (switch off at the wall) and ends with a clear engineer recommendation. Its weakness is that it drifts into 'the drain pump itself is failing' and keeps asking for checks the customer had already declined. Conversation 1 does stay uncertain between pressure switch and pump, which suits the case, but it overwhelms the customer, invents a 'WTG 7100' model and gives odd advice (a 90C empty wash, opening a tap to relieve water pressure, foam fixes when she uses a measured pod). It also pushes internal pressure-tube checks she had said she would not do. Neither asks about the flash pattern or the full model number.
